Our core database storage engineering committee published an Architectural Decision Record adopting synchronous group commit with direct NVMe I/O over asynchronous in-memory replication for transactional durability. Our previous distributed database acknowledged transaction commits immediately after writing into kernel page cache, deferring disk flushing to background daemons. A sudden power failure across 3 storage node servers corrupted the active write-ahead log and resulted in the loss of 150 acknowledged customer banking transactions.

The Architectural Decision Record mandated synchronous group commit batching utilizing direct file access across 16 database partition node instances. When client threads issue commit requests, the write coordinator aggregates multiple transaction log records into contiguous 4096-byte blocks before issuing single disk flush operations to NVMe storage. Production fault injection testing demonstrated that group commit batching achieved complete crash durability while sustaining 35000 write operations per second with P99 latency below 8 milliseconds.
